metadata.topic: Nuclear Physics — Definition of the Nucleus
metadata.note: 3m: define 'nucleus of an atom'. 3-slot cloze: small(0.5m) / dense(0.5m) / protons and neutrons(2m). Key mark is the correct particles — electrons orbit outside the nucleus and must not appear.

question.name: CSEC Phy Jan 2022 Q6a — Define the Nucleus of an Atom
question.text:
What is meant by the term 'nucleus' of an atom? Complete the statement below:

The nucleus is the [[1]], [[2]], positively charged central part of an atom, which contains [[3]].
question.general_feedback:
The nucleus:

The nucleus is the small, dense, positively charged central part of an atom, which contains protons and neutrons.

  • Small: The nucleus is approximately 10⁻¹⁵ m in diameter — about 100 000 times smaller than the atom itself.
  • Dense: Almost all the mass of the atom is concentrated in the nucleus.
  • Positively charged: Due to the protons (each carrying +1 charge). Neutrons are neutral.
  • Electrons are NOT in the nucleus — they orbit in shells outside the nucleus.

ddwtos.cloze_html: The nucleus is the [[1]], [[2]], positively charged central part of an atom, which contains [[3]].

groups.label: Nucleus is ___ relative to the atom
groups.diagnostic_hint: The nucleus is very SMALL — it occupies only about 10⁻¹⁵ m, while the atom is about 10⁻¹⁰ m. The nucleus is roughly 1/100,000th the size of the atom.

groups.label: Nucleus is very ___ for its size
groups.diagnostic_hint: The nucleus is extremely DENSE — almost all of the atom's mass is concentrated in the tiny nucleus. Nuclear density is approximately 2.3 × 10¹⁷ kg/m³.

groups.label: Nucleus contains ___
groups.diagnostic_hint: The nucleus contains PROTONS and NEUTRONS (collectively called nucleons). Electrons orbit the nucleus but are NOT in the nucleus. The number of protons = atomic number.

ddwtos.word_bank_note: 13 tokens for 3 slots. Slot 1 (small): 'large' and 'diffuse' describe the electron cloud (the atom as a whole); the nucleus is tiny. Slot 2 (dense): 'light' is wrong — the nucleus is very dense (almost all atomic mass is here). 'empty' describes the space between nucleus and electrons. 'negative' is wrong — the nucleus is positively charged. Slot 3 (protons and neutrons / nucleons): Both accepted — 'nucleons' is the collective term for protons and neutrons. 'Protons only' ignores neutrons (hydrogen-1 is the only exception). 'Protons, neutrons AND electrons' is wrong — electrons are NOT in the nucleus (this is the pre-Rutherford 'plum pudding' model). 'Electrons and protons' is also wrong for the same reason.
